note: The THIRD phase-1 metric, built 27 Aug 2026 to predict the saturation split the workload regression exposed and nothing then computed could see. No new solves -- the eleven temperature fields were already on disk.
the_split_it_explains: Efficiency retained as demanded margin grows 3 K -> 8 K divides the eleven shapes almost binarily: six retain 97.7-100%, five retain 37.4-53.5%, nothing between. It is NOT ordered by plateau width -- turbo (plateau 15) and turbo_idle (19) retain ~98% while fpu4 (12) collapses to 43%.
definition: hot_region_depth(temps, fraction=0.05): the temperature drop from the peak to the coolest of the hottest `fraction` of blocks. A share of blocks, not a count, so it transfers across floorplans with different block counts.
against_the_existing_metrics: Neither separates the split at all. relative_plateau_25pct overlaps by 30 blocks IN THE WRONG DIRECTION (rho -0.647); peak_to_runner_up_gap_K overlaps by 1.8 K and is not significant (rho +0.391, p 0.23). The gap cannot see it because it looks at the top TWO blocks; the plateau cannot because it counts blocks rather than measuring how fast temperature falls.
mechanism: As the demanded margin grows the plan must reach further down the distribution. Where temperature falls away steeply below the top few per cent there is a well-defined hot group and cooling stays efficient. Where it falls away shallowly the plan meets an ever-widening set of near-peak blocks and efficiency collapses.

robustness.note: the split survives cleanly from fraction 0.02 to 0.20, so 0.05 is not delicate

status: Validated on ELEVEN WORKLOADS, one floorplan. It has NOT been tested across floorplans -- the constant-power sweep left only two convergent dies, too few to regress. That is the next test, and it is the same transfer question relative_plateau has already passed.
